children: shares fell more than 15% in extended trading on Wednesday after the anti-inflammatory drug developer announced that its lead candidate, EVO756, failed to meet its main goals in a mid-stage trial for patients with eczema.

Citing topline data, the Palo Alto, California-based biotech said that EVO756 did not meet the primary and secondary endpoints in a Phase 2b trial targeting adults with moderate-to-severe eczema, an inflammatory condition also known as atopic dermatitis.
The dose-ranging study for 121 adults with moderate-to-severe AD was designed to evaluate the oral treatment over a 12-week treatment period with its follow-up extending through Week 14.
None of the doses under investigation met the trial's main goals, the company said, adding that given the setback, it no longer plans to further study EVO756 in AD.
